criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo identifies LTV exceeds 80% FFIEC supervisory limit
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo notes in A-7 that the as-is LTV of 81.04% 'exceeds customary supervisory LTV guidance for acquisition, development and construction lending,' but it does not identify the 80% supervisory LTV limit under FFIEC / 12 CFR Part 365 (or equivalent federal interagency guidelines). The criterion requires an explicit identification of the 80% regulatory threshold, which is absent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo recommends board exception approval for LTV exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo addresses the LTV exceedance in Section A-7, noting the as-is LTV of 81.04% exceeds customary supervisory LTV guidance for ADC lending. It expressly references the need to confirm whether the loan committee or board approved exceptions to standard underwriting guidelines, and recommends obtaining the credit approval, including any documented exception and its mitigants, before closing. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage includes specific CREC covenant for vapor barrier
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains an explicit, specific covenant addressing vapor barrier maintenance. Section 11.1(b) requires Mortgagor to 'Maintain, preserve, and keep in good condition and working order the vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7,' and not to penetrate or compromise it without SCDHEC/Lender approval. Section 11.1(c) adds an annual inspection obligation, 11.1(a) prohibits residential use of the Bay 1 ground floor, and Article 11 expressly ties these obligations to the Land Use Restriction recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, RMC Office (SCDHEC Site ID No. SC-29403-0772). The obligation is reinforced in Sections 6.6, 8.2(k), 8.9, and 11.2 (no modification of the Land Use Restriction), with a corresponding Event of Default at Section 14.1(k). This far exceeds the generic 'comply with environmental laws' standard the criterion identifies as insufficient.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage prohibits residential conversion of ground floor Lot 7/Bay 1
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly prohibits residential use or conversion of the ground floor of Lot 7 / Bay 1. Section 6.6 states Mortgagor shall not convert the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1) to residential use or permit any inconsistent use, and Section 11.1(a) separately prohibits residential use or any use inconsistent with the SCDHEC Land Use Restriction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Breach of CREC/environmental restriction is an event of default
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.1(k) of the mortgage expressly makes failure to comply with Article 11 or the SCDHEC Land Use Restriction an Event of Default, specifically referencing the vapor barrier maintenance obligation beneath the Bay 1 slab and any violation or modification of the restriction. Article 11 itself imposes both the vapor barrier maintenance covenant (§11.1(b)) and the prohibition on residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (§11.1(a)), and §14.2(c) confirms such breaches trigger an immediate Event of Default without a cure period. The restriction is therefore directly tied to a default provision.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Memo identifies CREC compliance obligation as a drafting issue
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum extensively discusses the CREC on Lot 7 (off-site petroleum contamination at 518 King Street), the SCDHEC No Further Action letter and Land Use Restriction, and the vapor barrier as an institutional control (see Section I, items I-1 through I-4, and Top-Risk Register item I-3). Critically, it expressly identifies these as requiring specific environmental covenants in the Mortgage beyond a standard environmental compliance clause: it implements Title Commitment closer's notes ¶1 and Requirement 6 via a dedicated Article 11 with LUR-specific covenants (no residential use of Bay 1 ground floor, vapor barrier maintenance and annual inspection, SCDHEC notice/approval, no modification of the LUR), plus a no-cure Event of Default for LUR violations (§§14.1(k), 14.2(c)) and a conditioned Permitted Exception in Exhibit B. It also flags the ESA recommendation for a pre-acquisition vapor barrier inspection and a draw condition for Bay 1 slab work. This squarely satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo identifies renovation holdback gap ($900K shortfall)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum identifies the renovation holdback gap in Section F-4: it states that the $2,250,000 holdback against the $3,150,000 renovation budget leaves $750,000 of hard costs plus $150,000 of soft/contingency, totaling $900,000 to be funded by Borrower equity. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Mortgage requires borrower equity contribution before holdback draws
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's renovation disbursement provisions expressly address borrower equity sequencing. Section 8.2(g) conditions each holdback advance on evidence that Mortgagor's equity contribution allocable to the Renovation Budget 'has been or is being funded on a pro rata, pari passu basis' with Lender's advances, such that the ratio of aggregate Lender advances to aggregate Mortgagor equity contributions (measured against completed work) does not exceed the ratio of the Renovation Holdback to Mortgagor's equity contribution set forth in Exhibit C. Section 8.2(a) further requires each draw request to specify 'the amount of Mortgagor's equity funds expended or concurrently expended' for the applicable line items. Exhibit C, paragraph (c) reinforces this, requiring pro rata, pari passu funding at a maximum 2.5:1.0 lender-to-equity ratio, with a certified reconciliation delivered with each draw request, and Exhibit C (d)/Section 8.5 require the borrower to fund any overruns from its own funds. While the structure is pro rata rather than strict 'equity-first,' the criterion expressly permits provisions that 'otherwise address[] the sequencing of borrower equity vs. lender holdback draws to protect the lender,' and these provisions do so by ensuring borrower equity is contributed alongside each advance and before the lender's exposure exceeds the agreed ratio.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo flags draw schedule shows interspersed (not equity-first) funding
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo addresses the sequencing issue in F-4 ('The Holdback covers only 78.9% of hard costs; no pari passu or equity-first requirement is in the Term Sheet... Nothing prevents the Borrower from front-loading its equity and exhausting it before the Bank's holdback is drawn — the draw schedule actually does the reverse — or from being unable to fund its share at the point of maximum spend'), noting the absence of any equity-first/pari passu requirement and that the schedule does not front-load equity. F-2 further breaks out lender draws and borrower draws per category across the fourteen monthly draws, confirming that equity is drawn alongside (interspersed with) lender advances. F-1 and the executive summary expressly quantify the resulting squeeze: at month 11 'Only $130,000 of lender holdback remains with $180,000 of budgeted costs remaining,' with borrower equity ending at −$5,000 — i.e., the holdback is nearly exhausted before completion. The criterion's two elements (interspersed rather than equity-first funding, and holdback-exhaustion risk before completion) are both present.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Memo identifies Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 conflict with leasing covenants
criteria_results.reasoning: Section C-3 of the memorandum expressly identifies that Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC holds a right of first refusal on Bay 2 (which the memo treats as vacant throughout, e.g., the 56.13% occupancy analysis and Bay 2 lease-up TI/commission projections). It explains the ROFR's mechanics (15 business days to match a bona fide third-party offer, surviving renewal under the First Amendment) and that 'the appraisal adjusts its lease-up timeline by 60–90 days for it, and the rent roll workbook flags that marketing is constrained' — i.e., that the ROFR constrains the Borrower's ability to lease the vacancy. It draws two drafting consequences: disclosure as a representation (§4.1(p), Schedule 4.1(n) note (2)) and a tenant acknowledgment/waiver (§5.8) so the ROFR does not burden Lender's remedies, and C-6 cross-references the leasing covenant (§5.6) that governs renewals. This satisfies the criterion: the ROFR on the vacant Bay 2 and its constraining effect on lease-up/marketing (and hence the leasing covenant) are discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Mortgage addresses ROFR in leasing covenant provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly acknowledges the Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 as an existing tenant right in Section 4.1(p) and Schedule 4.1(n), and Section 5.8 further addresses required tenant acknowledgments regarding that ROFR. Therefore it does not contain a standard leasing covenant with no reference to or accommodation of the existing ROFR.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Memo identifies missing assignment consent clause in Lowcountry Provisions lease
criteria_results.reasoning: Section C-1 of the memorandum is expressly devoted to this issue: it identifies that the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease for Bay 1 'has no assignment, estoppel, SNDA or attornment provision,' citing the Lease Abstracts ('Assignment/Subletting: No provision. Lease is silent'), the Rent Roll Summary note, the appraisal, and the Term Sheet conditions precedent. It then analyzes the implications for the lender's assignment of rents in detail — enforceability against the tenant under the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act (with a correction to the statutory citation to S.C. Code Ann. § 29-3-610 et seq.), the tenant's lack of any contractual cooperation/consent obligation at enforcement, and the absence of subordination/attornment (risk that the lease survives foreclosure). It also specifies the drafting responses adopted (representations as to authority to assign rents, tenant direction authority, post-closing covenant to obtain an amendment). The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage/memo recommends estoppel certificate from Lowcountry Provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The Mortgage expressly requires tenant estoppel certificates as an ongoing covenant in Section 5.8 (and Section 7.7/5.8 address the Lowcountry Provisions lease specifically, requiring Mortgagor to use diligent efforts to obtain estoppel/SNDA and an amendment at first renewal), and the Issues Memorandum separately recommends obtaining estoppels from all three tenants, singling out Lowcountry Provisions in item C-1 (High) and in the diligence request list (C-1/C-2/C-3). Estoppel certificates tied to the rent assignment/tenant acknowledgment are thus present in both documents, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage includes borrower representation re right to assign rents
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.7 of the mortgage expressly contains a borrower representation and warranty: "Mortgagor represents and warrants that it has the full right, power, and authority to assign the Leases and Rents as provided in this Article 7, and that no consent of any tenant is required for such assignment under any Lease or applicable law." This directly addresses the borrower's authority to make the assignment of rents, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo identifies gap between SPE requirements and operating agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: Section D-1 of the memorandum expressly identifies that the borrower's operating agreement lacks the required SPE and bankruptcy-remoteness provisions — no independent manager whose vote is required before a voluntary bankruptcy filing, no separateness covenants, no single-purpose restriction on the broad purpose clause, and no bankruptcy-remoteness/consent language — citing the Operating Agreement Summary §§1.4, 3.1, 3.2 and Term Sheet §10.1(g). It is ranked Critical in the Top-Risk Register and the memo recommends and specifies a form of Operating Agreement Amendment (adding the Independent Manager requirement, separateness covenants, single-purpose restriction, and unanimous-consent requirement for bankruptcy/dissolution/merger), to be executed by all three members and made a condition precedent to closing. The gap and needed amendments are thoroughly discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Mortgage includes SPE covenants with independent director requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes explicit single-purpose entity covenants in Article 6, including Section 6.3, which requires an Independent Manager meeting independence criteria and requires that manager's vote/consent before bankruptcy, insolvency, dissolution, or similar actions. This satisfies the criterion for an independent director/manager requirement for bankruptcy remoteness.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo flags need for passive member consent to SPE restrictions
criteria_results.reasoning: Section D-1 expressly states that the Operating Agreement Amendment adding the Independent Manager, separateness, single-purpose and bankruptcy-remoteness provisions must be executed by all three members — GDG, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC — and made a condition precedent to closing; it further analyzes the OA §9.1 amendment mechanics (75% threshold, GDG 72% + Harborline 10% would suffice procedurally, but recommends all three signatures because the covenants must bind each member, and notes the proviso requiring consent of any member whose economic rights are altered). Section 7(g) reiterates that the amendment is the likely flashpoint because it requires all three members and alters governance rights the passive members bargained for. The need for passive-member consent/joinder is therefore clearly discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Mortgage includes flood insurance covenant for $5M in Zone X
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes Article 10, Section 10.1(c) 'Flood Insurance,' requiring flood insurance on the Property in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000), naming Lender as mortgagee and loss payee. It also expressly references that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X and that Lender requires the coverage as a condition of the Loan. This matches the criterion exactly (flood insurance covenant for $5M in Zone X).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Memo or mortgage distinguishes contractual vs. regulatory flood insurance
criteria_results.reasoning: Both documents make the distinction. The issues memorandum, item H-2, expressly states that flood coverage in Zone X is 'a credit requirement, not a regulatory one,' notes the $5,000,000 requirement is permissible but that the compliance file should record 'it is a credit decision and that no federally mandated flood insurance or escrow requirement is engaged,' with a cross-reference to B-9. The mortgage itself, Section 10.1(c), states that 'Lender requires flood insurance as a condition of the Loan notwithstanding that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X and that federal law may not require flood insurance for property in that zone,' and separately mandates compliance with federal flood requirements only if a later determination places any portion in a Special Flood Hazard Area. No presentation of the requirement as federally mandated.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Memo identifies balcony encroachment over King Street ROW
criteria_results.reasoning: Section B-5 of the memorandum is expressly titled 'Balcony encroachment over the King Street right-of-way' and states that Title Commitment Schedule B-II Exception 5 discloses a ~2.5-foot encroachment over the King Street ROW, recommends ALTA 28.1 coverage, notes that no City encroachment permit or license is in the record, and recommends obtaining the encroachment permit/license (or written confirmation that none is required) and an ALTA 28.1 endorsement quote. It further addresses the renovation scope work over the right-of-way requiring City/BAR approval and includes related Mortgage provisions (§§5.5, 8.9, 16.1(e)). This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Mortgage includes covenant to maintain encroachment permit/license
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage addresses the King Street balcony encroachment only partially. Section 8.9(c) requires Mortgagor to 'obtain all permits, approvals, and licenses required by the City of Charleston for any work within or over the King Street right-of-way, including any encroachment permit or license relating to the decorative iron balcony,' but this is a one-time covenant tied to the Renovation Work, not an ongoing covenant to maintain any required encroachment permit/license in force throughout the loan term. Moreover, the document contains no covenant expressly prohibiting Mortgagor from exacerbating, enlarging, or extending the encroachment (the only related items are a general compliance-with-laws covenant in Section 5.5, a Lender-consent requirement for alterations in Section 6.6, a permitted-exception description in Exhibit B, and a balcony-related indemnity in Section 16.1(e)). Because the criterion requires both a covenant to maintain the encroachment permit/license and a covenant not to exacerbate the encroachment, the output does not satisfy it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula specifies which U.S. Treasury rate is used
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the 'Treasury Rate' in Section 1.1 with specificity: it is the yield to maturity of the U.S. Treasury security having a maturity closest to (but not later than) the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period, as reported in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15, with linear interpolation between the two nearest published maturities if no exact match exists, and reference to the most recent prior publication if H.15 is unavailable. Section 13.3 uses this defined Treasury Rate as the discount rate for computing the Yield Maintenance Premium. This is a specific reference identifying which Treasury rate/maturity is used, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula includes the 50 basis point spread
criteria_results.reasoning: The yield maintenance formula in Section 13.3 calculates the present value using the Treasury Rate as the discount rate and does not reference or add a 50 basis point spread. No 50 bps spread is included in the formula.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula provides a calculable methodology
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.3 provides a detailed yield maintenance formula: the premium is the greater of 1% of the prepaid principal or the excess of the present value of remaining scheduled principal and interest payments through the end of the Yield Maintenance Period over the outstanding principal. It identifies the discount rate as the Treasury Rate, defines how the Treasury Rate is determined (including interpolation), and specifies monthly discounting and final-payment adjustment. This is sufficiently calculable from the formula alone.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Memo identifies yield maintenance ambiguity in term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies yield maintenance ambiguity in the Term Sheet, including the ambiguous placement of the 50 bp spread (E-2) and the undefined Treasury rate tenor (E-5), and explains that the formula must be made specific and deterministic in the Mortgage to avoid an indefiniteness or unenforceable-penalty challenge, including under South Carolina law (E-7).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Mortgage transfer restrictions cover indirect/fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.4 includes 'Change of Control' language expressly capturing indirect/upstream changes, including transfers of interests in Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP or its general partner (Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or successor), and transfers of ownership interests in Harborline Capital Advisors LLC, along with direct and indirect changes in Mortgagor's members/managers. This satisfies the criterion requiring indirect/fund-level transfer restrictions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Memo identifies transfer restriction gap re fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo's Section D-2 expressly identifies the gap. It quotes Term Sheet §10.3's 10% individual / 25% aggregate restriction with the existing-member exception, then explains that the OA confirms the restriction is entity-level only and does not reach upstream changes in member entities. It specifically cites OA §4.2(c) allowing Tidewater GP to transfer to 'any successor fund' and gives illustrations including Tidewater GP Holdings being acquired and Harborline's internal ownership changing entirely, concluding the 72% controlling interest could pass without consent. It then adopts a Change of Control definition covering GDG, Tidewater GP Holdings/successor GP and Harborline levels, and D-6 adds diligence on Tidewater/Harborline entities. This satisfies the criterion directly.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: 'Existing members' exception is narrowly defined
criteria_results.reasoning: The transfer restriction’s 'existing members' exception is not left vague: Section 6.3 expressly identifies the three existing members as Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC, and Section 6.4 limits the exception to transfers among members existing as of the Closing Date, subject to notice and no Change of Control. This closed-class and Change-of-Control limitation adequately prevents unintended loopholes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Memo identifies tight timeline between completion and DSCR testing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the timing gap: it states the DSCR testing begins at month 24 while the interest-shortfall guaranty and substantial completion occur at month 14, leaving months 15–24 (approximately 10 months) unsupported; J-1 quantifies the ~$457,000 gap. It also shows current in-place income is far short of the 1.25x DSCR (0.285x amortizing / 0.371x IO) and that even best-case stabilized NOI yields only 0.554x, so the lease-up window and insufficiency of in-place income are discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Mortgage includes DSCR cure mechanism or cash sweep provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes an express DSCR cure/protective mechanism. Section 12.2 establishes a 1.25x DSCR covenant tested at DSCR Testing Dates but grants Mortgagor a 30-day cure right: upon Lender's notice, Mortgagor may deposit a calculated 'Cure Amount' into a DSCR Cure Reserve (equal to the excess of Annual Debt Service over NOI divided by 1.25), which is treated as reducing Annual Debt Service for the Measurement Period and restores compliance; the cure right is available twice during the Loan term. Section 9.4 (DSCR Cure Reserve) implements the mechanics, applying reserved funds to upcoming installments (including interest-only installments) in inverse order of maturity without triggering prepayment premiums. Additionally, Section 9.7 provides a cash-management/deposit-account-control trigger upon any failure to satisfy the DSCR covenant, and Section 14.1(i)/14.2(c) make clear that only an uncured failure constitutes an Event of Default. Thus the DSCR covenant is not a bare hard default; it has both a reserve/equity-cure mechanism and a cash-management protective provision. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Memo identifies chain of title concern for vacated Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum's Section B-1 (Critical) expressly identifies that the Anson Lane strip was conveyed by the City of Charleston by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128, Page 443, with 'no warranties of title,' notes the chain-of-title disclaimer and inconsistent descriptions, and recommends obtaining written confirmation from Prestige Title/Commonwealth National that the strip will be insured as part of the legal estate, plus quotes for affirmative coverage/endorsements. The quitclaim/chain-of-title concern and the title insurance coverage recommendation are both fully addressed, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Mortgage legal description includes Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's legal description in Exhibit A expressly includes Parcel Two, the vacated Anson Lane strip, identifying City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 and the quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443. The strip is also referenced in the granting clause and defined terms.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies lender name as Calverley Heritage Bank
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's preamble explicitly names the lender as 'CALVERLEY HERITAGE BANK, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation,' and the lender's acceptance signature block also identifies 'CALVERLEY HERITAGE BANK.' The lender name is therefore correctly identified.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies lender entity type and address
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's preamble identifies the lender as 'CALVERLEY HERITAGE BANK, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, having its principal office at 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, Georgia 31401' — matching the required entity type and address exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies borrower name as Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage identifies the borrower/Mortgagor as 'PALMETTO GATEWAY PARTNERS LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company' in the preamble and signature block.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies borrower entity type and address
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage preamble identifies the borrower as 'PALMETTO GATEWAY PARTNERS LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company, having its principal office at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401.' Both the entity type (South Carolina LLC) and the principal office address match the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct loan amount of $14,750,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage consistently states the loan amount as $14,750,000.00. Recital A states the original principal amount of the Loan is 'Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($14,750,000.00).' Recital B similarly states the Note is in that amount, Section 3.1 caps the secured principal at $14,750,000.00, and the title policy requirement in Section 5.13 is also $14,750,000.00. This matches the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct maturity date of April 15, 2030
criteria_results.reasoning: The Mortgage defines the "Maturity Date" in Section 1.1 as "April 15, 2030, being the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Closing Date," and the Closing Date is stated as April 15, 2025. This matches the required maturity date of April 15, 2030 (5 years from closing).

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states interest rate as Daily SOFR + 285 bps
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the Applicable Spread as 285 bps (2.85%) but does not state the interest rate as Daily SOFR plus 285 basis points. The benchmark is only referenced indirectly via 'SOFR Floor Rate' and the rate in effect under the Note; 'Daily SOFR' is missing. Therefore the benchmark is not correctly stated as required.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states SOFR floor of 3.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: In Article 1.1, the defined term "SOFR Floor Rate" is expressly stated as "three percent (3.00%) per annum," and the 3.00% floor is also referenced in the "Annual Debt Service" definition. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct default rate: applicable rate + 5.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.5 expressly defines the Default Rate as the otherwise applicable rate of interest under the Note plus five percent (5.00%) per annum, which matches the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month interest-only period from closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The Mortgage expressly defines an Interest-Only Period commencing on the Closing Date (April 15, 2025) and ending on April 15, 2027, which is exactly 24 months. It also states that monthly installments of interest only are due during that period.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 25-year amortization schedule after IO period
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the Interest-Only Period and expressly references a 25-year amortization schedule in the Annual Debt Service definition, calculating level monthly principal and interest payments on that schedule. The schedule is included and is consistent with the post-interest-only structure; no incorrect amortization term is stated.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month lockout period with no prepayment
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines a 24-month Lockout Period from the Closing Date and Article 13.1 prohibits prepayment in whole or in part during that period, stating Mortgagor has no right to prepay and any purported prepayment is void unless Lender elects otherwise. This satisfies the 24-month no-prepayment lockout requirement.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes yield maintenance premium prepayment from month 25 through month 48
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly provides a yield maintenance prepayment phase from month 25 through month 48. Section 13.2 is titled 'Yield Maintenance Period' and permits prepayment during the Yield Maintenance Period (defined as months 25 through 48 following the Closing Date) subject to payment of the Yield Maintenance Premium. The definitions section confirms this: 'Yield Maintenance Period' means the period commencing on the first day of the twenty-fifth (25th) month following the Closing Date and ending on the last day of the forty-eighth (48th) month following the Closing Date. Section 13.3 sets forth the Yield Maintenance Premium formula (greater of 1.00% of principal prepaid or present value of remaining payments discounted at the Treasury Rate). The timing matches the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes open prepayment with no premium during final 12 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines an Open Prepayment Period from the first day of the 49th month through the Maturity Date, i.e., months 49–60/final 12 months, and Section 13.4 permits prepayment in whole or in part without any prepayment premium, penalty, or yield maintenance amount.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes late charge of 5% with 10-day grace period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.5 expressly provides for a late charge equal to 5.0% of any monthly installment of principal and/or interest not received within ten (10) calendar days after the due date, satisfying the stated criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes DSCR covenant of at least 1.25x tested quarterly
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes Section 12.2 requiring a DSCR of not less than 1.25x, and defines DSCR Testing Dates as the last day of each calendar quarter beginning after the specified initial period, so the covenant is tested quarterly. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage DSCR testing commences 24 months after closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the DSCR Testing Date as the last day of the first full calendar quarter ending after the date 24 months following the Closing Date, and specifically identifies the first DSCR Testing Date as June 30, 2027, with testing upon quarterly reporting around July 30, 2027. Since the Closing Date is April 15, 2025, 24 months later is April 15, 2027, and June 30, 2027 is the quarter-end following month 24. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes tax and insurance escrow provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.1 (Tax and Insurance Escrow) expressly requires Mortgagor to deposit with Lender on the Closing Date and on the first day of each calendar month thereafter 'an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual real property taxes and casualty and liability insurance premiums for the Property,' with provisions for holding, applying, adjusting, and curing deficiencies. This fully satisfies the criterion, and the defined term 'Tax and Insurance Escrow' is used consistently throughout (e.g., Sections 2.2(d), 9.5, and the Net Operating Income definition excludes escrow deposits from Operating Expenses).

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes capital replacement reserve of $0.25/SF/year
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.2 expressly establishes a Capital Replacement Reserve requiring monthly deposits of $645.83, described as one-twelfth of $7,750.00, calculated at $0.25 per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet. This matches the criterion exactly, including the equivalent annual and monthly amounts.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes TI/LC reserve with $150,000 initial deposit
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.3 establishes a Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve requiring a $150,000 initial deposit on the Closing Date and replenishment to the full $150,000 from Mortgagor's own funds after any disbursement. This matches the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes renovation reserve/holdback of $2,250,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The output explicitly provides for a $2,250,000 Renovation Holdback in Recital C (with the $12,500,000 Initial Advance summing to the $14,750,000 Loan), and Article 8 governs disbursement on a draw basis. Section 8.2 specifies the required conditions, including a certified AIA G702/G703 application and Architect certification of completed work, conditional and unconditional lien waivers from the GC and subcontractors/suppliers, and a title date-down endorsement confirming no intervening liens (plus future-advance coverage). Frequency, 10% retainage, change-order limits, cost-overrun funding, and Substantial Completion requirements are also addressed. The holdback amount is correct and the draw conditions match the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes initial advance of $12,500,000 at closing
criteria_results.reasoning: Recital C explicitly states an initial advance of Twelve Million Five Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($12,500,000.00) to be made on the Closing Date, and Section 3.1/2.1 confirm the Initial Advance is part of the secured obligations. The figure matches the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage legal description includes Lots 7, 8, and 9 of Hampstead Village Plat
